//: FIP: diameter 6.35-6.77 cm, mass 56.0-59.4 g, 2.54 m drop must bounce 135-145 cm (altitude ball 122-135 cm above 1000 m). dragCoefficient: free-flight C_D of new felt balls, 0.507 +- 0.024 at 14-30 m/s whatever the spin (Cross & Lindsey, 128 shots; wind tunnels read 15-20% high). spinDecayPerM: k in dw/dt = -k w v (spin decay is linear in spin x speed, James & Haake 2008); k estimated from golf's ~4%/s at 60 m/s and felt balls decaying about six times faster, so a ball loses about 0.5% of its spin per metre flown at sea level (scaled by air density). wear: the match ball's nap fluffs up and its pressure leaks with every impact (each counts (normal speed / 15 m/s)^2, at most 3). dragFluff: used balls fly with 4.1% more drag than new ones (Hawk-Eye, 9,200 Davis Cup first serves: C_D 0.603 used vs 0.579 new), reached over fluffImpacts (in AI doubles a point is about 15 weighted impacts, so the nap is fluffed up within the first set, as a tennis ball is by its 9-game change). pressureLoss: the fraction of restitution lost over pressureImpacts (padel balls lose pressure and soften in play, IBV endurance test of 10 brands for Testfakta; no measured curve, so this is tuning: a 150-point match, about 2,200 weighted impacts, takes the 2.54 m drop from about 140 to 136 cm).

altitude.name: Altitude ball (lower pressure, for venues above 1000 m)
